sources.entry: SensibleSideButtons - Make mouse side buttons work for back and forward in more apps. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/archagon/sensible-side-buttons)

summary.name: SensibleSideButtons
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that makes third-party mouse side buttons work as back/forward navigation in most apps, by sending a synthetic three-finger swipe gesture to the view under the cursor.
use_cases: Make mouse side buttons go back and forward in browsers and other apps on macOS
Avoid menu bar blinks and alert sounds from rebinding side buttons to Cmd+[ and Cmd+]
Navigate history in Finder, Xcode documentation and other apps with a third-party mouse
Learn how macOS swipe gestures and event taps can be used to remap mouse buttons
summary.what_it_does: SensibleSideButtons lives in the macOS menu bar and intercepts the M4 and M5 side button clicks using a CGEventTap. It replaces each click with a synthetic three-finger swipe gesture, which macOS delivers to the view under the cursor, so back and forward work in practically any app with a history. The author says the app uses no CPU polling and only sends system events when a side button is clicked. Users can enable or disable it from the app menu.
notable: Sends navigation to the view under the cursor rather than the foreground app, avoiding stray keyboard shortcuts
Uses a fake three-finger swipe gesture reverse-engineered from Logitech MX Master behavior
Open source under GPLv2 with source on GitHub
Written natively in Objective-C/Xcode with a small event tap
caveats: Only works on macOS; the page describes no other platforms
Depends on the legacy three-finger swipe navigation setting being enabled in Trackpad preferences, since the gesture is emitted through it
Author notes the author's own experience only; compatibility with every app is not guaranteed
